description: Take St Basil's Cathedral apart piece by piece in 3D, and read the story of Ivan the Terrible's victory church: nine chapels on one foundation, the blinded-architect legend, and the most painted silhouette in Russia.

intro: Ivan the Terrible ordered it built to celebrate taking Kazan, and gave Moscow a building like nothing in a thousand years of Byzantine tradition: nine churches fused into one, crowned with onion domes, hiding a labyrinth inside. This is the story of the cathedral the world pictures when it pictures Russia.
page_title: St Basil's Cathedral: Exploded 3D Model and History | Architectural Atlas

sections.body: In 1552 Ivan IV, the Terrible, took Kazan, the Tatar stronghold on the Volga, and then Astrakhan. To commemorate the victories he ordered a votive church on Red Square, and from 1555 to 1561 the architects Ivan Barma and Postnik Yakovlev raised it: the Cathedral of the Intercession of the Most Holy Theotokos on the Moat, consecrated on 12 July 1561. Their names were only recovered in the 19th century, found in a 17th-century manuscript. It was built of brick, then a new material for Russian churches, which had traditionally used limestone.
sections.heading: Ivan's victory church

sections.body: The plan has no parallel in Russian architecture. Nine independent chapels stand on a single foundation of about 1,680 square meters: eight side churches arranged around the central Church of the Intercession, the four larger ones octagonal on the compass points, the four smaller ones cuboid on the diagonals, so that the whole forms an eight-pointed star. The largest, the central Intercession church, is 46 meters tall inside but its floor covers only 64 square meters. Inside, the chapels are joined by a labyrinth of narrow vaulted corridors. In 1588 a tenth chapel was added over the grave of the venerated holy fool Vasily, St Basil the Blessed, and his shrine was so popular that its name swallowed the cathedral's: the Intercession Cathedral became St Basil's.
sections.heading: Nine churches, one foundation

sections.body: How tall is it? Modern listings give 47.5 meters, but the cathedral museum's own chief curator cites 65 meters as the historical height, which fits the record neatly: in 1600 the Ivan the Great Bell Tower overtook it by 16 meters, and the bell tower stands 81 meters tall. Either way, until 1600 it was the tallest building in Moscow, and the skyline belonged to its bonfire of domes.
sections.heading: The 65-meter question

sections.body: The best-known story about the cathedral is also its most suspect. Legend says Ivan was so delighted by the finished building that he had the architects blinded, so they could never design anything to surpass it. It is a great story and almost certainly just that: the architects' names survive in the written record, and nothing in the sources supports the blinding. Like the labors on the Brandenburg Gate or the chariot race that was never run in the Colosseum, the wrong fact is the interesting one: the legend says more about how Europe imagined Ivan than about how Barma and Postnik ended their days.
sections.heading: The architects Ivan blinded?

sections.body:
St Basil's is one of the most popular cultural symbols of Russia, and the default establishing shot whenever film or television needs to say Moscow. Soviet newsreels put it in the background of the May Day military parades marching through Red Square, fixing the silhouette in the world's mind. The 19th-century French traveler the Marquis de Custine, seeing it for the first time, compared it to the scales of a golden fish and the enameled skin of a serpent, and wondered whether the men who worshipped in this box of confectionery work could be Christians. In 2008 Russia voted it one of the Seven Wonders of Russia, and UNESCO had already listed it, with the Kremlin and Red Square, in 1990.

Gamers know it from an unlikely quarter: in the Command and Conquer: Red Alert universe the cathedral stands on Red Square as the iconic Moscow landmark, defended in the Allied campaign and obliterated by prism tanks in Operation Chrono Storm. Between the newsreels, the games and a thousand establishing shots, the bonfire of domes may be the most reproduced silhouette in architecture.

timeline.text: Ivan the Terrible takes Kazan; Astrakhan follows.
Construction begins on Red Square to Barma and Postnik's design.
The Cathedral of the Intercession is consecrated.
The tenth chapel is added over the grave of St Basil the Blessed.
The Ivan the Great Bell Tower overtakes the cathedral as Moscow's tallest building.
UNESCO lists the Kremlin and Red Square as World Heritage.
Russia votes St Basil's one of the Seven Wonders of Russia.
